name: vscode-translucent
description: A Visual Studio Code extension that applies a native translucent backdrop effect to the editor window on Windows 11.

vscode-translucent.opacity.description: Default background opacity of the workbench UI (0 = fully transparent, 1 = opaque).

vscode-translucent.surface.color.markdownDescription: **One colour for the whole window.** Tints every outer surface once (editor, sidebars, activity bar, panel, title bar, status bar) and clears everything that sits on top of them (tabs, section headers, the search box, gutters and so on), so nothing is painted twice. Use a see-through colour, e.g. `#0a0f0c33`. With this set, the panel glass settings work best at 1. Layers, accent and text colours are applied on top, so those are the only things you customise. Leave empty to keep the theme's colours.

vscode-translucent.surface.borderColor.markdownDescription: The colour of the dividers between panels (sidebar, activity bar, panel, split editors, title and status bars) when a surface colour is set. Empty = no lines (`#00000000`). Lines inside panels and around controls are cleared; resize handles, focus rings and highlights keep the accent.

vscode-translucent.layers.enabled.markdownDescription: Put a tinted, partly see-through surface under the things you read and type in, so text doesn't float over whatever is behind the window. Changes apply immediately; no reload.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Warm brown layers, forest-green accents, green menu text.
Neutral dark layers, fairly solid. Leaves your theme's accents alone.
Nothing preset: only the layers you set below.
vscode-translucent.layers.preset.markdownDescription: Starting point for the layers below. Anything you set yourself overrides the preset.

vscode-translucent.layers.inputs.color.markdownDescription: **Inputs (text boxes, chat boxes, search fields)**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.inputs.opacity.markdownDescription: **Inputs (text boxes, chat boxes, search fields)**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.menus.color.markdownDescription: **Menus and dropdowns**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.menus.opacity.markdownDescription: **Menus and dropdowns**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.widgets.color.markdownDescription: **Editor flyouts (hover, suggestions, find)**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.widgets.opacit.markdownDescription: **Editor flyouts (hover, suggestions, find)**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.quickInput.col.markdownDescription: **Command palette and quick pick**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.quickInput.opa.markdownDescription: **Command palette and quick pick**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.notifications..markdownDescription: **Notifications**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.
**Notifications**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.tabStrip.color.markdownDescription: **Editor tab strip**: colour of the layer. Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.layers.tabStrip.opaci.markdownDescription: **Editor tab strip**: how solid the layer is, from `0` (clear) to `1` (solid). Leave unset to use the preset's.

vscode-translucent.settingsPage.color.markdownDescription: **Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts and extension pages**: colour of the page behind them. Needs a window reload (you'll be asked).

vscode-translucent.settingsPage.opacity.markdownDescription: **Settings, Keyboard Shortcuts and extension pages**: how solid that page is, from `0` (off, fully see-through) to `1` (solid). Try `0.85`.

vscode-translucent.layers.softBorders.markdownDescription: Swap the theme's dark lines and shadows for clear or faint ones: the border beside the scrollbar, the terminal panel's top edge, and scroll and widget shadows. On a see-through window these show up as black streaks. Changes apply immediately.

vscode-translucent.accent.color.markdownDescription: One colour for every accent: activity-bar icons, section headers, tab underline, links, cursor, scrollbars, selection, badges. Faint accents keep their faintness. Chat colours are left alone. Leave unset to use the preset's; set it to an empty value to keep your theme's accents.

vscode-translucent.text.menuColor.markdownDescription: Text colour in menus (right-click and menu bar).

vscode-translucent.text.remoteIndicatorC.markdownDescription: Text colour of the remote indicator in the status bar (for example **WSL: Ubuntu**).

vscode-translucent.text.activeIconColor.markdownDescription: Colour of the **selected** icon in the activity bar (side or top). The other icons keep the accent colour.

vscode-translucent.text.remoteIndicatorB.markdownDescription: Background of the remote indicator in the status bar. Use the colour picker's transparency slider for a tint (for example `#1b1420d9`, plum at 85%).

vscode-translucent.text.remoteIndicatorH.markdownDescription: Background of the remote indicator when you hover over it.

vscode-translucent.editorContainerBackgr.description: Background opacity of the editor container (0 = fully transparent, 1 = opaque).

vscode-translucent.leftSidebarContainerB.description: Background opacity of the left sidebar container (0 = fully transparent, 1 = opaque).

vscode-translucent.rightSidebarContainer.description: Background opacity of the right sidebar (auxiliary bar) container (0 = fully transparent, 1 = opaque).

vscode-translucent.editorContainerBorder.description: Controls whether the editor container border is visible.

vscode-translucent.leftSidebarContainerB.description: Controls whether the left sidebar container border is visible.

vscode-translucent.rightSidebarContainer.description: Controls whether the right sidebar (auxiliary bar) container border is visible.

vscode-translucent.editorContainerBorder.description: Border radius (rounding) of the editor container (e.g. '0px', '8px', '12px').

vscode-translucent.leftSidebarContainerB.description: Border radius (rounding) of the left sidebar container (e.g. '0px', '8px', '12px').

vscode-translucent.rightSidebarContainer.description: Border radius (rounding) of the right sidebar (auxiliary bar) container (e.g. '0px', '8px', '12px').

vscode-translucent.activityBarContainerB.description: Controls whether the side activity bar container border is visible.
Background opacity of the side activity bar container (0 = fully transparent, 1 = opaque).

vscode-translucent.activityBarContainerM.description: [Experimental] Margin around the side activity bar container (e.g. '0px', '8px', '10px 0').

vscode-translucent.activityBarContainerG.description: [Experimental] Gap between the side activity bar container and the workspace (e.g. '0px', '8px').

vscode-translucent.activityBarContainerB.description: Border radius (rounding) of the side activity bar container (e.g. '0px', '8px', '12px').

vscode-translucent.extensionFixes.claude.markdownDescription:
**Claude Code:** show the text in the IN/OUT tool boxes. Its panel fades long output with a mask made from the panel background, which hides everything when that background is see-through.

This edits Claude Code's own installed files (a backup is kept, and turning this off puts it back). It is checked again whenever extensions change, so it survives Claude Code updates.

vscode-translucent.extensionFixes.antigr.markdownDescription:
**Antigravity:** make the chat panel see-through instead of black, and give its input box and message bubbles the **Inputs** layer colour. The panel then loads its chat page through a small local proxy that adds the colours.

This edits Antigravity's own installed files (a backup is kept, and turning this off puts it back). It is checked again whenever extensions change, so it survives Antigravity updates.

vscode-translucent.extensionFixes.claude.markdownDescription:
**Claude Code:** a thin bar in this colour down the left edge of your own messages, so they stand apart from Claude's replies without a filled bubble. Leave empty for none.

This edits Claude Code's own stylesheet (a marked block that is taken out again when you clear this). It is checked again whenever extensions change, so it survives Claude Code updates.

**Claude Code:** a dot in this colour before each of your own messages, in the same column as the dots before Claude's replies (your messages move in to line up with them). Leave empty for none.

Like the bar, this is a marked block in Claude Code's stylesheet, re-applied after updates and taken out when cleared.

**Claude Code:** the background of the band behind each of your messages and of the IN/OUT tool boxes. Claude paints both with the editor colour, so on a tinted see-through editor they show as a second, darker layer. `#00000000` makes it flush with the editor. Leave empty to keep Claude's own.

A marked block in Claude Code's stylesheet, re-applied after updates and taken out when cleared.

**Claude Code:** a backing colour for your message when Claude pins it to the top of the panel while you scroll. On a see-through window the pinned message otherwise sits on top of the text scrolling under it. A partly see-through colour (e.g. `#221716e6`) keeps the glass look; the area behind it is also blurred. Leave empty for none.

A marked block in Claude Code's stylesheet, re-applied after updates and taken out when cleared.

vscode-translucent.applyToJupyterNoteboo.description: Forces `--vscode-notebook-editorBackground` to transparent for Jupyter and VS Code Notebook editors.
